notes: Lease-vs-license dispute over Coney Island candy-stand concession stalls; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding-house issue.

holding_summary: The court held that an 1887 restrictive covenant barring 'apartment houses' did not prohibit erection of a 15-story apartment hotel with small kitchen-less suites and centralized management, because such a building was akin to a hotel rather than the family-housekeeping structure the covenant targeted. It also held that renting suites for lengthy periods alongside transient accommodations does not convert a building into a prohibited apartment house.

quotes.text: The fact that apartment hotels may rent small suites for somewhat lengthy periods, in addition to providing for possible transient accommodations, does not convert them into apartment houses as such, especially as many of our regular hotels furnish similar facilities for permanent guests.
An apartment hotel like the one here proposed is akin to a hotel and not to an apartment house.

notes: Restrictive-covenant construction case; letting practice (transient + lengthy-period suites) upheld as not converting the building into a prohibited apartment house.

holding_summary: The court held that 'The Lucerne,' an apartment building whose suites were rented under annual leases without soliciting transient tenants, was not a 'hotel' within the meaning of the 1895 civil-rights statute. Because it was an ordinary letting of apartments rather than innkeeping, the proprietor could lawfully exercise the ordinary landlord's right to select tenants and refuse to lease to the plaintiff.

quotes.text: These apartments are rented upon annual leases and transient tenants are not solicited.

Tested by this definition “ The Lucerne ” is certainly not an hotel, and when the defendant refused to lease apartments to the plaintiff it exercised only the right which every landlord .undoubtedly has to ’make his own selection of tenants.

A house where all who conduct themselves properly, and who are able and ready to pay for their entertainment, are received, if there is accommodation for them, and who, without any stipulated engagement as to the duration of their stay, or as to the rate of compensation, are, while there, supplied at a reasonable charge with their meals, their 'lodging, and such services and attention as are necessarily incident to the use of the house as a temporary home.

notes: Turns on the duration-of-stay test distinguishing hotel/innkeeping from ordinary annual apartment letting; letting treated as ordinary incident of ownership giving proprietor tenant-selection discretion.
Ordinary apartment-house landlord/tenant dispute over house rules and constructive eviction from noise; no lodging/short-let issue.
Innkeeper liability for a stolen horse left in the stable; concerns guest/inn status for property bailment, not compensated human occupancy of a dwelling.

court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, First Department
notes: Dispute over who was landlord (trustee vs. association) under a printing-plant lease; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Tort case on landlord's duty to repair and liability for a tenant's guest injured by a falling ceiling; does not bear on legality/character of letting.
Private alley easement/right-of-way dispute among adjoining lot owners with old private-stable restrictions; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting.
Trade-name/unfair-competition suit between an apartment house and a hotel both named 'Apthorp'; describes but does not adjudicate the legal character of the letting arrangements.
Tenant-at-will use-and-occupation claim over former woolen-mill factory buildings; no dwelling/lodging issue.

Tenement House Law fire-escape/fire-safety case turning on whether a building was 'intended, arranged or designed' for three-family occupancy; concerns family occupancy classification, not compensated lodging or boarding-house regulation.
Fire-insurance 'vacant and unoccupied' forfeiture clause dispute; owner's husband slept in the house between tenancies, no compensated occupancy at issue.

holding_summary: The Appellate Term reversed a judgment for a tenant who had leased an apartment-hotel suite for a year and stopped paying rent after learning the hotel also let rooms to transient guests. The court held that letting some rooms to transients did not breach any covenant of quiet enjoyment absent an express restriction in the written lease confining the building to non-transient apartment use.

quotes.text: There is not, however, the slightest proof in the case that the renting of rooms to transients in any degree interfered with defendant's beneficial enjoyment of the rooms rented to him.

but it seems to me, if he intended to have his tenancy conditional upon such an exclusive occupancy of the building, he should not have executed the lease unless it contained a clause safeguarding his rights in that respect, and clearly expressing the agreement in that behalf between the parties.

notes: Affirms hotel operator's right to let rooms to transient guests alongside annual-lease tenants absent an express restrictive covenant.
Holdover-tenant/lease-termination dispute over a factory building; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Same trade-name dispute as case_id 2808585 (Astor 'Apthorp' apartment house vs. hotel), reported in a different reporter; unfair-competition holding, not a letting-legality holding.
Breach of covenant for quiet enjoyment via wrongful ejectment suits over a leased printing office; commercial lease, not dwelling/lodging.

School-tuition residency/domicile case; family rented ordinary apartment rooms as tenants for a school year. Retrieved on an in-passing citation to a boarding-house-keeper case (Stacom v. Moon), but the holding itself does not adjudicate letting/lodging legality.
Splitting-a-cause-of-action rule for rent claims arising from a municipal tenancy-from-year-to-year; procedural rent litigation, not lodging/short-let doctrine.
